title: Former Cecil County deputy sheriff sentenced for illegal searches on police database
summary: A former Cecil County deputy sheriff was sentenced Tuesday to eight years in prison with all but six months suspended for illegal searches on a police database, according to the Maryland State Prosecutor’s Office.
content:
by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters November 19, 2025

by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters November 19, 2025

A former Cecil County deputy sheriff was sentenced Tuesday to eight years in prison with all but six months suspended for illegal searches on a police database, according to the Maryland State Prosecutor’s Office.

After Donta Odom completes his sentence, he will serve three years of supervised probation.

The sentencing by Cecil County Circuit Court Judge Paul M. Bowman comes after Odom pleaded guilty last month to four counts of misconduct in office and three counts of unauthorized access to a computer.

A statement of facts said Odom searched a law enforcement database for information on seven people who were not suspects, including his wife.

The document states Odom also searched information on romantic partners, relatives of romantic partners, a woman who worked in his building and others. Authorities said Odom had no “legitimate law enforcement reason to search” a database about any of the individuals, who are not named.

Odom worked for sheriff’s office from 2019 until he resigned in August 2025.

GET THE MORNING HEADLINES.

One of those searches Odom did between September and December 2024 on a person identified as “Victim 4.”

In December of that year, after Odom and Victim 4 went on a vacation to Ocean City, Victim 4 informed the sheriff’s office of Odom’s conduct.

Although Odom was served with a no-contact order, he continued to contact Victim 4 through social media, texts and emails. In addition, Odom secretly recorded a conversation with Victim 4 in March of this year, when they met at a secluded location, leading to a wiretapping charge.

On March 9, 2025, Odom repeatedly asked Victim 4 why she told investigators certain information. The next day, Odom texted her, “Why don’t you ask for the no contact order to be dropped” and “to delete everything.”

Odom also spoke with Victims 1 and 2 prior to and after they were interviewed by investigators.

“You have done incalculable harm to law enforcement. You have truly dishonored the badge you used to wear,” Bowman said, accordihg to a news release from the prosecutor’s office. “Your unlawful behavior while serving as a police officer will not be tolerated.”

“Law enforcement officers have access to sensitive and confidential information necessary to discharge their official duties,” Maryland State Prosecutor Charlton T. Howard III said in the statement. “Our office will continue to do our best to ensure that those officers who abuse their positions of trust and misuse their authorities for corrupt reasons are held accountable.”
